description: Patch releases of Send are automerged here. Send keeps no schema of its own to migrate: an upload is a Redis hash carrying the owner token, the client-side metadata blob, the download limit and a storage prefix, given a TTL of at most `send_environment_variable_max_expire_seconds` (7 days by default), plus one opaque file named `<days>-<id>` under the storage backend. There is no migration machinery anywhere in the image - `server/` of registry.gitlab.com/timvisee/send:v3.4.27 contains no migration code, and the upstream tree has no migrations directory - so a restarted container cannot rewrite anything an operator holds, and whatever it does not understand expires on its own within the week.

Measured rather than assumed across the four most recent patch spans: v3.4.23...v3.4.24, v3.4.24...v3.4.25, v3.4.25...v3.4.26 and v3.4.26...v3.4.27 touch the browser bundle, the localisation files and `server/config.js`, and every `server/config.js` change in that range adds a new key with a default rather than renaming or removing one. Nothing in those diffs touches the storage or Redis layers.

Worth spelling out because it cuts the other way: upstream has not bumped Send's minor version since 3.4.0, so 'patch' here is not a conservative slice of the release stream, it is the whole of it - v3.4.24 through v3.4.27 span 2023 to 2025 and include user-visible work such as the customisable notices and the Thunderbird sponsorship banner. Automerging patches therefore means automerging every release upstream realistically ships. That is acceptable for this role because none of it can touch operator data, and because the Molecule run does considerably more than watch the unit turn active: it asserts that the process reports the version the role pins and runs the image the role configures, that `/config` reports the limits and dropdown defaults the role's `env` file rendered, that `/__heartbeat__` answers 200 (the only endpoint that pings Redis - `/`, `/config`, `/__version__` and `/__lbheartbeat__` all answer 200 with Valkey stopped), and that a real upload over the WebSocket API lands its metadata in Valkey and its blob under the role's own data path. A bump that broke startup, configuration parsing, the Valkey connection or the storage path fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out of that decision. registry.gitlab.com/timvisee/send publishes 202 tags, of which 35 are real `vX.Y.Z` releases; the other 167 are the per-commit `master-<sha>` tags and a floating `latest`, none of which parse as semver and none of which Renovate will follow.

Upstream is quiet rather than dead, and that is worth knowing before trusting this automation: the last release, v3.4.27, is from 2025-07-01, and the GitLab project (github.com/timvisee/send is a mirror of it) has seen no commits since. Automerge costs nothing while that lasts; if it lasts much longer, the question for this role becomes whether to keep shipping Send at all rather than whether to automerge it.
